tls_enabled.title: TLS Enabled
tls_enabled.description: Whether TLS encryption is enforced on the management server configuration update channel. False indicates plaintext (HTTP/raw TCP) is permitted or used.

minimum_tls_version.title: Minimum TLS Version Enforced
minimum_tls_version.description: The minimum TLS/SSL protocol version the management channel will accept during handshake negotiation. Values below TLS 1.2 expose the channel to downgrade and decryption attacks. Used by both transport encryption and downgrade rules.

enabled_cipher_suites.title: Enabled Cipher Suites
enabled_cipher_suites.description: List of cipher suites enabled on the management server TLS endpoint. Presence of weak or export-grade ciphers (RC4, DES, 3DES, NULL, EXPORT, anon) exposes configuration traffic to decryption or downgrade.

client_certificate_authentication_requir.title: Client Certificate Authentication Required (mTLS)
client_certificate_authentication_requir.description: Whether the management server requires devices to present a valid client TLS certificate (mutual TLS) during connection establishment, preventing unauthorized device connections and MITM attacks.

device_server_certificate_validation_enf.title: Device-Side Server Certificate Validation Enforced
device_server_certificate_validation_enf.description: Whether endpoint devices are configured to validate the management server's TLS certificate against a trusted CA, preventing devices from connecting to impersonated management servers.

replay_protection_mechanism.title: Replay Protection Mechanism
replay_protection_mechanism.description: The type of replay protection mechanism embedded in configuration update messages to prevent retransmission attacks.

replay_token_server_side_validation_enab.title: Server-Side Replay Token Validation Enabled
replay_token_server_side_validation_enab.description: Indicates whether the management server actively validates replay protection tokens (nonces, timestamps, sequence numbers, session tokens) on inbound messages and rejects duplicate or out-of-order messages.

message_timestamp_window_seconds.title: Message Timestamp Acceptance Window (Seconds)
message_timestamp_window_seconds.description: The maximum age in seconds of a configuration update message timestamp the server or device will accept. A value of 0 means timestamps are not enforced; excessively large values render replay protection ineffective.

payload_integrity_mechanism.title: Payload Integrity Mechanism
payload_integrity_mechanism.description: The cryptographic mechanism applied to configuration payloads independent of transport layer security, such as HMAC, AEAD, or digital signatures attached to each message.

tls_terminated_at_intermediary.title: TLS Terminated at Intermediary
tls_terminated_at_intermediary.description: Indicates whether TLS is terminated at an intermediary component (load balancer, reverse proxy, service mesh sidecar) before the configuration payload reaches the endpoint device, creating an internal plaintext segment.

endpoint_validates_payload_integrity.title: Endpoint Validates Payload Integrity
endpoint_validates_payload_integrity.description: Whether the receiving endpoint device independently verifies the cryptographic integrity of the configuration payload (e.g., validates HMAC or signature) before applying the configuration, separate from TLS handshake validation.

certificate_validation_mode.title: Certificate Validation Mode
certificate_validation_mode.description: The mode used by the device or management client to validate server TLS certificates. 'full' means full chain and hostname validation; 'skip_hostname' disables hostname verification; 'skip_expiry' skips expiry; 'disabled' bypasses all validation.

accepted_certificate_types.title: Accepted Certificate Types
accepted_certificate_types.description: The types of server certificates the device or management client will accept for the TLS connection. Accepting self-signed, expired, or hostname-mismatched certificates indicates validation weaknesses.

certificate_pinning_enforced.title: Certificate Pinning Enforced
certificate_pinning_enforced.description: Whether the device or management client enforces certificate pinning (pinned public key or certificate fingerprint) for the management server TLS connection, preventing acceptance of certificates from arbitrary CAs.

downgrade_attack_protection_enabled.title: TLS Downgrade Attack Protection Enabled
downgrade_attack_protection_enabled.description: Whether explicit downgrade protection mechanisms are configured, such as TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV signaling or equivalent server-side rejection of fallback hello requests.

rate_limiting_enabled.title: Rate Limiting Enabled on Management Channel
rate_limiting_enabled.description: Whether the management server enforces rate limiting on incoming configuration update requests to prevent flooding attacks.

max_update_requests_per_minute.title: Maximum Update Requests Per Minute Per Source
max_update_requests_per_minute.description: The configured threshold for the maximum number of configuration update requests allowed per source per minute. A value of 0 indicates no limit is set.

source_authentication_required.title: Source Authentication Required for Update Requests
source_authentication_required.description: Whether the management server requires authenticated device identity before accepting configuration update requests, limiting unauthenticated flood attempts.

rpki_validation_enabled.title: RPKI Route Origin Validation Enabled
rpki_validation_enabled.description: Whether Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) route origin validation is enforced on the upstream BGP peers carrying management server IP prefixes, rejecting RPKI-invalid routes.

bgp_prefix_filter_configured.title: BGP Prefix Filters Configured for Management IP Ranges
bgp_prefix_filter_configured.description: Whether explicit BGP inbound prefix-lists or route filters are configured on border routers to reject more-specific route advertisements for management server IP ranges from unauthorized autonomous systems.

management_ip_ranges_publicly_routed.title: Management Server IP Ranges Are Publicly Routed
management_ip_ranges_publicly_routed.description: Whether the management server IP address ranges are reachable via the public internet routing table, as opposed to being confined to private RFC1918 space or a dedicated out-of-band management network.

dnssec_validation_enabled.title: DNSSEC Validation Enabled
dnssec_validation_enabled.description: Whether the device or its DNS resolver enforces DNSSEC validation when resolving the management server hostname, preventing acceptance of unsigned or tampered DNS responses.

management_server_certificate_pinning.title: Management Server Certificate Pinning Mode
management_server_certificate_pinning.description: Whether the device enforces certificate pinning or strict CA validation when connecting to the management server after DNS resolution, limiting the impact of DNS-based redirection to a rogue server.

management_hostname_resolution_method.title: Management Server Hostname Resolution Method
management_hostname_resolution_method.description: How the device resolves the management server address, indicating whether resolution is protected against spoofing via static configuration or dependent on potentially unprotected DNS.

sensitive_data_in_headers.title: Sensitive Data Transmitted in HTTP Headers
sensitive_data_in_headers.description: Whether authentication tokens, API keys, device identifiers, or policy parameters are transmitted in HTTP headers or query strings rather than exclusively in the encrypted request body.

header_logging_enabled.title: Full HTTP Header Logging Enabled on Network Appliances
header_logging_enabled.description: Whether network appliances, proxies, or access logs capture full HTTP headers including Authorization and custom secret-bearing headers, persisting sensitive values to log storage.

session_token_rotation_enabled.title: Session Token Rotation Enabled
session_token_rotation_enabled.description: Whether the management server rotates session tokens periodically or after significant events to limit the window of opportunity for token hijacking.

session_token_max_lifetime_seconds.title: Session Token Maximum Lifetime (Seconds)
session_token_max_lifetime_seconds.description: The maximum duration in seconds that a management session token remains valid without requiring re-authentication or rotation. Long-lived tokens increase hijacking risk.

session_binding_mechanism.title: Session Binding Mechanism
session_binding_mechanism.description: The mechanism used to bind a management session token to the originating client, preventing token reuse from a different context.

update_channel_network_isolation.title: Update Channel Network Isolation Method
update_channel_network_isolation.description: The network isolation mechanism in place for management update traffic, indicating whether it is separated from untrusted or user traffic.

update_traffic_colocated_with_user_traff.title: Update Traffic Co-located with User or Untrusted Traffic
update_traffic_colocated_with_user_traff.description: Indicates whether management update traffic traverses the same physical or logical network segment as user-facing or untrusted traffic, increasing interception and injection risk.

acl_restricts_update_channel_access.title: ACL Restricts Update Channel Access
acl_restricts_update_channel_access.description: Indicates whether access control lists or firewall rules restrict which hosts can communicate on the management update channel, limiting lateral movement risk on shared segments.

payload_compression_enabled.title: Payload Compression Enabled
payload_compression_enabled.description: Whether configuration update payloads are compressed (e.g., DEFLATE, gzip, zstd) before or during encryption in the update channel. True indicates compression is applied, creating oracle attack surface.

attacker_can_inject_partial_content.title: Attacker Can Inject Partial Known Content Into Payload
attacker_can_inject_partial_content.description: Whether an attacker can influence or inject partial known plaintext into the compressed-then-encrypted configuration payload (e.g., via cross-origin requests, SSRF, or partial update fields they control), required to mount a compression oracle.

ciphertext_length_observable.title: Ciphertext Length Observable to Attacker
ciphertext_length_observable.description: Whether the attacker can observe the byte length of the encrypted configuration response (e.g., via network sniffing, side-channel in a shared network, or length-revealing API responses). Length observability is the core oracle requirement for CRIME/BREACH attacks.
